title: Series vs Parallel Explorer
description: Two identical LEDs with 220 ohm resistors, rewired between a series chain and two parallel branches. The scope plots one branch current against the total current the battery supplies, making Kirchhoff's current law visible as two separating lines.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Electronics
Electric Circuits
Series Circuits
Parallel Circuits
Kirchhoff's Laws
prerequisites: Voltage, current and resistance as quantities
How breadboard rows and rails are connected

controls.label: Start/Pause
controls.purpose: run or freeze the animation and the plot

controls.label: Series / Parallel
controls.purpose: rewire the same two LEDs between the two topologies

controls.label: Supply voltage
controls.purpose: vary the supply and watch each topology respond differently

simulationModel.type: DC node-voltage analysis with iterative nonlinear element resolution
equations: Kirchhoff's current law at every net
I = (Va - Vb - Vf) / R per branch
assumptions: Every frame is DC steady state
LEDs use a fixed forward voltage plus a small series resistance
Components are ideal - no tolerance, temperature, or wire resistance
limitations: No transient response - no charging or discharging over time
Capacitors are open circuits, so RC timing is not modelled
No inductance and no AC sources
Transistor current gain (beta) is not modelled
